content.inline:
# Smart contracts on Convex

Contracts are **actors**: accounts with their own address, balance, private state and callable functions, written in Convex Lisp and run by the CVM. Reads are free queries; deploying, and calling functions that change state, are transactions (accounts child for costs and signing).

## Deploy

```clojure
(deploy
  '(do
     (def counter 0)
     (defn ^:callable increment []
       (set! counter (+ counter 1))
       counter)))
```

- `^:callable` (or `^{:callable true}`) is the only way to export a function; plain `def`s are private state, updated with `set!`.
- `deploy` returns the new address. A vector of forms composes library builders: `(deploy [(@convex.fungible/build-token {…}) (@convex.fungible/add-mint {…})])`.
- `(set-controller #ADDR)` decides who may upgrade the actor.

## Call and use libraries

- `(call #ACTOR (increment))` from a transaction; the caller pays the juice and any memory the actor allocates.
- Reach libraries through CNS, never a hard-coded address: `(@convex.fungible/balance #TOKEN #HOLDER)`. **Never use `import` in query or transaction source** — it mutates the account and costs juice every time.

## Tokens

- Fixed supply: `(deploy (@convex.fungible/build-token {:supply 1000000}))`
- Mintable: compose `add-mint` into the same deployment and **always set `:max-supply` explicitly**; the choice is permanent.
- `balance`, `total-supply` and `decimals` are queries; `transfer`, `mint` and `burn` are transactions. Minting must satisfy the token's `:minter` trust monitor, else `:TRUST`.

## Access control — trust monitors

Authorisation is a check of subject, action and object: `(@convex.trust/trusted? monitor *caller* :mint)`. A bare address trusts only itself; `nil` denies everything. Compose the standard monitors instead of hand-rolling logic — `(@convex.trust.monitors/all (permit-subjects #13 #17) (permit-actions :open :close))`; also `any`, `everyone`, `before`/`after`/`between`, `owns`, `delegate` (deny before allow). Fail with `:TRUST` on denial and keep action keywords literal at the call site.

## Errors you will meet

`:UNDECLARED` wrong function name · `:CAST` wrong type · `:ARITY` wrong argument count · `:STATE` invalid for the current state · `:TRUST` no rights · `:FUNDS` insufficient coins · `:JUICE` out of juice · `:MEMORY` out of allowance · `:NOBODY` no such account · `:COMPILE` bad source.

## Practice

Write against protocol version 1 semantics. Store the minimum on-chain and give actors clean-up functions — freed storage refunds allowance. Try an actor on a local or test network before Protonet: anything deployed there is real.
